correctness.rationale: The Nyström residual equals \(\det(A)(Ju)(Ju)^{\mathsf T}/(u^{\mathsf T}Au)\) in dimension two. Conditioning on the Gaussian sketch gives exact Rademacher variance \(4R_{12}^2\); isotropic Gaussian angular integration produces closed moments. Algebra gives the exact difference, the derivative of Q is strictly negative on \(t>1\), and equality and isotropic cases are explicitly addressed. Positive-definite high-dimensional strict reversals follow by dominated convergence. Standalone SymPy identities and 28 independent angular quadratures passed. Finite experiments are supportive, not the proof.

value.rationale: Gives a complete sharp basis-sensitive criterion for choosing between two prescribed equal-cost randomized trace estimators, with a unique spectral existence threshold. Unlike rotationally invariant Gaussian trace-estimator comparisons, the same fixed spectrum can reverse the risk ordering under coordinate rotation, with the reversal robust to small positive tails in every higher dimension. It clarifies when investing a matrix-vector product in Gaussian Nyström deflation is or is not productive under Rademacher residual probing, rather than merely presenting one cheap negative diagonal example.
